proposal.summary: 0x201d6-0x21270 is CM550's J1939 multiplexing input layer: it turns the j1939_received_* bytes that the six receive handlers store into engine inputs. Two tasks drive it: the 10 ms task 0x21070 runs the 17 two-bit switch inputs of j1939_input_signal_descriptor_table, the fan request, the retarder selection and five output-bit copies; the 50 ms task 0x21146 runs the accelerator inputs (low idle switch, idle switch pair, pedal position, remote accelerator) and the wet tank pressure. Each processor clears its input's bits in three one-dword bitmaps (0x800aa0 not-available data, 0x800aa4 message timeout, 0x800aa8 pedal input message timeout), tests its calibration enable bit and the module priority 0x808158 (e2m 12FE MXMOPZ) against the input's client priority, and then writes the override value (a switch's user value bit, an A/D channel's override word or a percent word) from the received byte, or the default when the message timed out or the value is not available. It is CM848's layer 0x509d98-0x50ae5c in the same address order: the nine bitmap helpers are step-for-step twins; the processors and the two tasks are counterparts, because CM848 adds the DM13 and monitor inhibit gates, a multiplex enable bit and a start delay and has its own fault bits, while CM550 has two processors CM848 lacks (remote accelerator, wet tank pressure) and files every fault under bit 0 of 0x806000.

functions.role: Clears bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa0.
functions.discriminator: It is the clear helper for 0x800aa0, the bitmap that 0x202d8 sets where a received value is 'not available' (a byte of 0xfb-0xfd or 0xff, a two-bit switch state of 3); its siblings 0x20210 and 0x2024a clear 0x800aa8 and 0x800aa4.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): clears bit N of j1939_input_data_error_bitmap (dword N >> 5 - mask 1 << (N & 31)), the bit that marks input N as delivering a not-available value. Each input processor calls it for its own input before it evaluates the input again. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x201d6) and CM848 (0x509d98): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x201da move.w (12,a7),d2; 0x201de-0x201e8 low byte sign-extended then lsr.l #5 = dword index; 0x201ea-0x201f8 mask = not (1 << (byte and 0x1f)); 0x20200 movea.l #0x800aa0,a0; 0x20206 and.l d2,(0,a0,d0.l*4). CM848 0x509d98: srawi r4,r3,5 / slw of 1 by r3 mod 32 / not / lwz - and - stw at 0x3fbd5a + 4 x index (lis r12,64; addi -17062). Step match: same index, same mask, same 32-bit and-store, base = the first of three consecutive dword bitmaps (CM550 0x800aa0 / a4 / a8 = CM848 0x3fbd5a / 5e / 62: +0 / +4 / +8 in both). Position: first of nine helpers that stand in the same order in both firmwares (clear +0 +8 +4, any +0 +8 +4, set +0 +8 +4: 0x201d6-0x20348 and 0x509d98-0x509f90). Call sites 0x2039a 0x20434 0x204d0 0x207a4 0x208c6 0x20e2e 0x20fc6 (retarder, fan, low idle switch, remote accelerator, switch entry, idle switch pair, wet tank); CM848's callers are the five of these processors that exist there. abs_refs: 0x800aa0 is referenced only at 0x20202 0x2028a 0x20302.

functions.role: Clears bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa8.
functions.discriminator: It is the clear helper for 0x800aa8, the bitmap that 0x20310 sets only for the accelerator inputs (6 low idle switch, 7 pedal position, 1 remote accelerator) when their message timed out, and whose 'any bit' result becomes the flag 0x80d70e.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): clears bit N of j1939_pedal_input_timeout_bitmap, the bit that marks an accelerator input's message as lost. Used for inputs 6 and 7 (accelerator low idle switch and pedal position) in both firmwares and for input 1 (remote accelerator) in CM550 only. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x20210) and CM848 (0x509dd8): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x20210-0x20248: the instructions of 0x201d6 with movea.l #0x800aa8,a0 (0x2023a) and and.l d2,(0,a0,d0.l*4) (0x20240). CM848 0x509dd8: the instructions of 0x509d98 on 0x3fbd62 (addi -17054), the +8 bitmap. Second of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x204e0 (low idle switch), 0x207b8 (remote accelerator), 0x20e42 (idle switch pair); CM848: the low idle switch and idle switch pair processors. abs_refs: 0x800aa8 only at 0x2023c 0x202a6 0x2033a.

functions.role: Clears bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa4.
functions.discriminator: It is the clear helper for 0x800aa4, the bitmap that 0x20348 sets exactly where an input's j1939_input_signal_timeouts word has reached 0.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): clears bit N of j1939_input_timeout_bitmap, the bit that marks input N's message as timed out (its j1939_input_signal_timeouts word reached 0). Each input processor calls it for its own input before it evaluates the input again. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x2024a) and CM848 (0x509e18): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x2024a-0x20282: the instructions of 0x201d6 with movea.l #0x800aa4,a0 (0x20274) and and.l (0x2027a). CM848 0x509e18: the instructions of 0x509d98 on 0x3fbd5e (addi -17058), the +4 bitmap. Third of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x203a2 0x2043a 0x204d8 0x207ae 0x208bc 0x20e38 0x20fd0 (the same seven processors as 0x201d6); CM848: the same five as its data error clear. abs_refs: 0x800aa4 only at 0x20276 0x202c2 0x20372.

functions.role: Returns 1 when the dword at 0x800aa0 is not zero, else 0.
functions.discriminator: It tests 0x800aa0 (the not-available data bitmap); 0x202a0 tests 0x800aa8 and 0x202bc tests 0x800aa4. Both input tasks call it first and turn its result into the fault bit.
functions.plate_comment: Returns 1 while any bit of j1939_input_data_error_bitmap is set (a loop over its one dword), else 0. Both J1939 input tasks call it and set or clear the data error fault from the result. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x20284) and CM848 (0x509e58): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x20284 clr.w d0 / clr.w d1; 0x20288 movea.l #0x800aa0,a0; 0x2028e tst.l (a0)+; not zero -> moveq #1,d0 (0x20292); zero -> addq.w #1,d1, tst.w d1, beq back to 0x2028e = a loop of one element; result in d0. CM848 0x509e58: li r4,0 / li r5,0; lwzx at 0x3fbd5a + 4 x r5; not zero -> li r4,1; else r5 + 1 and loop while r5 <= 0 (cmpwi r5,0; ble) = one element; extsh r3,r4. Fourth of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x210ce (10 ms task) and 0x2116c (50 ms task); CM848: cm848_processJ1939SwitchAndRequestInputs and cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorInputs.

functions.role: Returns 1 when the dword at 0x800aa8 is not zero, else 0.
functions.discriminator: It tests 0x800aa8 (the pedal input timeout bitmap). Its single caller, the 50 ms accelerator task, stores the result as 0 / 1 in the flag 0x80d70e.
functions.plate_comment: Returns 1 while any bit of j1939_pedal_input_timeout_bitmap is set (a loop over its one dword), else 0. Its one caller, the J1939 accelerator input task, stores the result in j1939_pedal_input_timeout_active_flag. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x202a0) and CM848 (0x509e98): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x202a0-0x202ba: the instructions of 0x20284 with movea.l #0x800aa8,a0 (0x202a4). CM848 0x509e98: the instructions of 0x509e58 on 0x3fbd62. Fifth of the nine helpers in both. One call site in each firmware: CM550 0x211dc, followed by move.b #1,(a2) / clr.b (a2) with a2 = 0x80d70e (0x211e6 / 0x211ee); CM848 0x50ae28 in cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorInputs, followed by stb to 0x40aaa8 - 0x80d70e and 0x40aaa8 are the same record, e2m 12F7 +2 MXACTMER.

functions.role: Returns 1 when the dword at 0x800aa4 is not zero, else 0.
functions.discriminator: It tests 0x800aa4 (the message timeout bitmap). Both input tasks call it second, after the data error test, and write the fault bit again from its result.
functions.plate_comment: Returns 1 while any bit of j1939_input_timeout_bitmap is set (a loop over its one dword), else 0. Both J1939 input tasks call it and set or clear the timeout fault from the result. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x202bc) and CM848 (0x509ed8): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x202bc-0x202d6: the instructions of 0x20284 with movea.l #0x800aa4,a0 (0x202c0). CM848 0x509ed8: the instructions of 0x509e58 on 0x3fbd5e. Sixth of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x21106 (10 ms task) and 0x211a4 (50 ms task); CM848: the same two tasks (bl 0x509ed8 at 0x50ac98 and 0x50adb8).

functions.role: Sets bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa0.
functions.discriminator: It is not a generic bit setter: the base 0x800aa0 is fixed in the code. Its eight call sites are exactly the 'not available' branches of the processors - byte values 0xfb-0xfd / 0xff and two-bit switch state 3 - never a timeout.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): sets bit N of j1939_input_data_error_bitmap: input N delivered a not-available value (a byte of 0xfb-0xfd or 0xff, or a two-bit switch state of 3) while its message is still arriving. The input tasks report any set bit as the data error fault. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x202d8) and CM848 (0x509f18): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x202d8-0x2030e: index and mask as 0x201d6 without the not; 0x20300 movea.l #0x800aa0,a0; 0x20306 or.l d2,(0,a0,d0.l*4). CM848 0x509f18: srawi / slw / lwz - or - stw at 0x3fbd5a + 4 x index. Seventh of the nine helpers in both. Call sites and the test before each: 0x20410 retarder (after cmpi.b #0xfe failed at 0x203fc), 0x204a2 fan, 0x20854 remote accelerator (0xff or 0xfb-0xfd, 0x2083e-0x2084e), 0x20e04 pedal position, 0x21062 wet tank, 0x20542 low idle switch (cmpi.b #3 at 0x20538), 0x20a46 switch entry (cmpi.b #3,(a0) at 0x20a3a), 0x20f9e idle switch pair. CM848's callers: the six of these processors that exist there. CM848's function_renames.csv header records that an earlier 'setBitInArray' twin at 0x4ef5c was removed as wrong; this is the real one.

functions.role: Sets bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa8.
functions.discriminator: It is the setter for 0x800aa8 and is called only for the accelerator inputs 6, 7 and 1, each time right after the timeout bit setter in the 'timer is 0' branch.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): sets bit N of j1939_pedal_input_timeout_bitmap: the message of an accelerator input was lost - input 6 or 7 (low idle switch, pedal position) in both firmwares, also input 1 (remote accelerator) in CM550. Always called together with setJ1939InputTimeoutBit. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x20310) and CM848 (0x509f54): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x20310-0x20346: the instructions of 0x202d8 with movea.l #0x800aa8,a0 (0x20338) and or.l (0x2033e). CM848 0x509f54: the instructions of 0x509f18 on 0x3fbd62. Eighth of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x2052c (input 6, after tst.w (0x804240).l found 0), 0x20808 (input 1, after tst.w (0x804236).l), 0x20cfe (input 7, after tst.w (0x804242).l); CM848: the low idle switch and pedal position processors.

functions.role: Sets bit N (the J1939 input number) of the one-dword bitmap at 0x800aa4.
functions.discriminator: It is the setter for 0x800aa4; every one of its seven call sites directly follows a tst.w of the input's j1939_input_signal_timeouts word that found 0.
functions.plate_comment: (J1939 input number): sets bit N of j1939_input_timeout_bitmap: input N's message timed out (its j1939_input_signal_timeouts word has counted down to 0). The input tasks report any set bit as the timeout fault. The same instructions and the same place in the layer in CM550 (0x20348) and CM848 (0x509f90): one shared name.
functions.evidence: CM550 0x20348-0x2037e: the instructions of 0x202d8 with movea.l #0x800aa4,a0 (0x20370) and or.l (0x20376). CM848 0x509f90: the instructions of 0x509f18 on 0x3fbd5e. Ninth of the nine helpers in both. Call sites 0x203d4 (after tst.w (0x80423e).l, slot 5), 0x2046a (0x804234, slot 0), 0x20524 (0x804240, slot 6), 0x207fe (0x804236, slot 1), 0x20986 (tst.w (0,a0,d0.w*2) on 0x804234 with the entry's slot), 0x20cf4 (0x804242, slot 7), 0x2100a (0x804246, slot 9); CM848's callers: the five of these processors that exist there.

functions.role: Converts the received J1939 engine retarder selection byte (input 5) into the retarder selection percent word, or loads the default and flags the input when its message timed out or the value is not available.
functions.discriminator: Input number 5: timer word 0x80423e, source byte 0x80d719 (j1939_received_engine_retarder_selection), scale x 4 / 10, output word 0x80d728 with the default 0x80815a and the client priority byte 0x80d726; its enable is bit 4 of algorithm_enable_flags_33_cal (0x803cd6), which no sibling reads.
functions.plate_comment: J1939 input 5, the engine retarder selection (EBC1 byte 5, j1939_received_engine_retarder_selection): while algorithm_enable_flags_33_cal bit 4 is set and j1939_input_source_priority is not below j1939_engine_retarder_selection_source_priority it writes j1939_engine_retarder_selection_percent = raw x 4 / 10 for a raw value up to 250. A timed out message (j1939_input_signal_timeouts[5] = 0), the error value 0xfe and a not-available value load j1939_engine_retarder_selection_default_percent instead; the timeout sets the input's timeout bit and a not-available value its data error bit. Called from the 10 ms J1939 input task (0x21070). The counterpart of cm848_processJ1939EngineRetarderSelection (0x509fcc), which adds the DM13 and monitor inhibit gates and takes its enable from word 13 bit 0.
functions.evidence: 0x20396 / 0x2039e clear data error and timeout bit 5 (bsr 0x201d6, 0x2024a); 0x203a8 move.w (0x803cd6).l,d0 / andi.w #0x10 / beq exit; 0x203b6-0x203c6 word 0x808158 against byte 0x80d726, blt exit; 0x203c8 tst.w (0x80423e).l; zero: 0x203d0 set timeout bit 5, 0x203da move.w (a3),(a2) = 0x80815a -> 0x80d728; 0x203e2 cmpi.b #0xfa,(a4) (a4 = 0x80d719): at most 250 -> lsl.l #2, divu.l #10, move.w d0,(a2); 0x203fc cmpi.b #0xfe -> default only; otherwise 0x2040a default and 0x2040c set data error bit 5. Called once: jsr at 0x21094. CM848 0x509fcc: the same steps and constants (li r3,5; cmpwi 250; slwi 2 / divwu 10; cmpwi 254; priority 0x5c340 against byte 0x40aac0; output 0x40aac2, default 0x5c342) plus lhz 0x40adda (DM13 flag) at 0x50a018 and lhz 0x40aaca (monitor inhibit) at 0x50a038 and 0x50a0a8, and the enable is lhz 0x3fd5b6 bit 0 (0x509fec). CM550's family has no operand for either flag (every absolute operand of 0x201d6-0x21270 was listed).

functions.role: Converts the received J1939 engine fan requested percent speed byte (input 0) into the fan request word, or loads the default and flags the input when its message timed out or the value is not available.
functions.discriminator: Input number 0: timer word 0x804234, source byte 0x80d71c (j1939_received_engine_fan_requested_percent_speed), scale x 16 / 10, output word 0x80d72a with the default 0x80815c and the client priority byte 0x80d727; its enable is bit 15 of algorithm_enable_flags_25_cal (0x803cc6).
functions.plate_comment: J1939 input 0, the engine fan requested percent speed (CM1 byte 1, j1939_received_engine_fan_requested_percent_speed): while algorithm_enable_flags_25_cal bit 15 (manual fan level override) is set and j1939_input_source_priority is not below j1939_engine_fan_request_source_priority it writes j1939_engine_fan_requested_speed = raw x 16 / 10 (0.25 percent per count) for a raw value up to 250. A timed out message (j1939_input_signal_timeouts[0] = 0), the error value 0xfe and a not-available value load j1939_engine_fan_requested_speed_default instead; the timeout sets the input's timeout bit and a not-available value its data error bit. Called from the 10 ms J1939 input task (0x21070); the output word has no reader in the dumped ROM. The counterpart of cm848_processJ1939EngineFanRequestedSpeed (0x50a0cc), which adds the DM13 and monitor inhibit gates.
functions.evidence: 0x20432 / 0x20438 clear data error and timeout bit 0; 0x20440 move.w (0x803cc6).l,d0 / andi.w #0x8000 / beq exit; 0x2044c-0x2045e word 0x808158 against byte 0x80d727, blt exit; 0x20460 tst.w (0x804234).l; zero: 0x20468 set timeout bit 0, 0x20470 move.w (a3),(a2) = 0x80815c -> 0x80d72a; 0x20478 cmpi.b #0xfa,(a4) (a4 = 0x80d71c): lsl.l #4, divu.l #10, move.w d0,(a2); 0x20492 cmpi.b #0xfe -> default only; otherwise 0x204a0 set data error bit 0 and 0x204a8 default. Called once: jsr at 0x2108e. abs_refs: 0x80d72a only at 0x20422. CM848 0x50a0cc: the same steps and constants (li r3,0; enable lhz 0x3fd5ce bit 15; priority 0x5c340 against byte 0x40aac1; slwi 4 / divwu 10; output 0x40aac4, default 0x5c344) plus the DM13 flag 0x40adda (0x50a11c) and the monitor inhibit flag 0x40aaca (0x50a13c, 0x50a180).

functions.role: Writes the received J1939 accelerator pedal low idle switch state (input 6) into the override value of logical switch 7, the idle switch, or the switch's default state when the value is error or not available.
functions.discriminator: Input number 6: it tests the timer word 0x804240 itself and writes only switch 7 (bit 7 of 0x80bcd8, priority byte 0x80bd4a + 7), setting the timeout and pedal input timeout bits 6 on a lost message. Its sibling 0x20e14 reads the same byte but writes both switches 7 and 8, tests no timer and needs the sampled throttle override bit as well.
functions.plate_comment: J1939 input 6, the accelerator pedal low idle switch (EEC2 byte 1 bits 1-2, j1939_received_accelerator_pedal_1_low_idle_switch), into logical switch 7, the idle switch: while the switch's override enable (algorithm_enable_flags_13_cal bit 7) is set and j1939_input_source_priority is not below switch_input_source_priority[7] it claims the switch and - at priority 0 - writes the switch's override value (switch_1_to_8_override_values bit 7): on for 1, off for 0, the default state bit (j1939_switch_input_default_state_bits bit 7) for 2 (error) and 3 (not available, which also sets the input's data error bit). A timed out message (j1939_input_signal_timeouts[6] = 0) sets the input's timeout and pedal input timeout bits and leaves the switch as it is. Called from the 50 ms J1939 accelerator input task (0x21146). The counterpart of cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorLowIdleSwitch (0x50a1b4), which adds the monitor inhibit gate and writes the switch through its priority helpers.
functions.evidence: 0x204cc-0x204e0 clear data error, timeout and pedal input timeout bit 6 (bsr 0x201d6, 0x2024a, 0x20210); 0x204e6 move.w (0x803cae).l,d0 / andi.w #0x80 / beq exit; 0x204f4-0x20500 word (a5) = 0x808158 against byte (7,a2) = 0x80bd51, blt exit; 0x20512 move.b (1,a5),(7,a2) (the priority word's low byte into the switch priority); 0x20518 tst.w (0x804240).l; zero: 0x20520 set timeout bit 6, 0x20528 set pedal input timeout bit 6, return; 0x20538 cmpi.b #3,(a4) (a4 = 0x80d71a): set data error bit 6 (0x2053e), then if (7,a2) is 0: move.l (0x807d6a).l,d0 / btst #7 -> ori.b #0x80,(a3) or andi.b #0x7f,(a3) (a3 = 0x80bcd8); 0x20572 cmpi.b #2: the same default write; else 0x205ac tst.b (a4) -> ori.b #0x80 / andi.b #0x7f. Called once: jsr at 0x2114e. CM848 0x50a1b4: li r3,6 three clears in the same order; enable lbz 0x3fdbce bit 7; priority 0x5c340 against 0x40c058 + 7; timer 0x3feab0; values 3 / 2 / else; default lbz 0x6456e bit 7; writes through 0x4ea40 / 0x4ea84 with (7, 0); plus the monitor inhibit flag 0x40aaca at 0x50a22c and 0x50a260.

functions.role: Sets the idle and not idle switch override values and throttle_above_idle_flag from local inputs: the raw sampled throttle A/D reading, or the debounced raw not idle switch.
functions.discriminator: The only function of the family that reads no J1939 byte and no timer: its sources are the QADC result register of the sampled throttle (0xfff2b0 + 2 x index, compared with 360 counts) and the raw not idle switch bit (0x80bced bit 0 XOR 0x800aaf bit 0) with the debounce timer 0x800aac and the previous state 0x800aae. Its one caller is the pedal position processor's timeout branch (0x20d0c). It reads an MC68336 register directly, hence the mc68k_ prefix.
functions.plate_comment: The local fallback for the idle validation switches while the J1939 pedal message is lost (its one caller is cm550_processJ1939AcceleratorPedalPosition on a timeout): it sets the override values of logical switch 7 (idle) and 8 (not idle) and throttle_above_idle_flag. With algorithm_enable_flags_25_cal bit 3 set (limp home on the analog throttle) it stores the sampled throttle's QADC result register in idle_check_accelerator_pedal_raw and takes more than 360 counts as off idle. Otherwise it debounces the raw not idle switch (switch_9_to_16_raw_values bit 0 XOR switch_9_to_16_polarity_bits_snapshot bit 0) with accelerator_idle_switch_debounce_timer (100, minus 50 per unchanged pass, applied at 0) and accelerator_idle_switch_previous_state. The counterpart of cm848_updateIdleSwitchesFromLocalInputs (0x50a2cc), which also has a debounce armed flag and writes the switches through its priority helpers.
functions.evidence: 0x205e0 move.w (0x803cc6).l,d0 / andi.w #8. Set: 0x205ee index = word 0x806be2 (sampled_throttle_sensor_config + 16, the QADC result register index), 0x205f8 move.w (0xfff2b0 + 2 x index),(0x80d72c).l, 0x20604 cmpi.w #0x168,(0x80d72c).l; at most 360: andi.b #0xfe,(1,a1) (0x80bcd9 bit 0 off), ori.b #0x80,(a4) (0x80bcd8 bit 7 on), clr.w (a3) (0x80aa86); above: the opposite and move.w #1,(a3). Clear: 0x20636 d2 = byte 0x80bced, 0x2063c-0x20652 (d2 XOR byte 0x800aaf) and 1; 0x20658 cmp.b (0x800aae).l,d2; different: 0x20698 store d2 in 0x800aae and move.w #0x64,(a2) (a2 = 0x800aac); same: tst.w (a2), subi.w #0x32,(a2), bgt exit, clr.w (a2), then the same two switch writes and the flag from d2. No priority test anywhere. One call site: 0x20d0c. 0xfff2b0 is referenced by only one other function, mc68k_processAnalogSensorChannels (0xb856). 0x80bced is the raw image byte of inputs 8-15: mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs stores it at 0x1502c before the polarity XOR at 0x15070. CM848 0x50a2cc: enable lhz 0x3fd5ce bit 3; analog branch cmpwi 360 with the result stored in 0x40aac6; switch branch reads cm848_readSwitchHardwareInput(8), previous state 0x3fbd68, timer 0x3fbd66 100 / minus 50; differences: the armed flag 0x3fbd69, a forced A/D reading option (0x3fdb78 bit 13) and writes through 0x4ea40 / 0x4ea84 at priority 0.

functions.role: (logical input, output number): copies one bit of the output image into the override value bit of one logical input when that input's override is enabled and the priority allows.
functions.discriminator: The only function of the family that reads the output image (0x80bcf6 + output / 8): its source is an output command bit, not a received J1939 byte, and it touches no timer and no fault bitmap. Both of its numbers are arguments; the 10 ms task calls it five times with constants.
functions.plate_comment: (logical input, output number): while the input's override enable bit is set (bit input + 208 of the algorithm enable words, that is words 13-17) and j1939_input_source_priority is not below switch_input_source_priority[output number] it claims the input and - at priority 0 - copies the output's bit of the output image (0x80bcf6 + output / 8) into the input's override value bit (0x80bcd8 + input / 8). The 10 ms J1939 input task (0x21070) calls it with (54, 1) (54, 4) (33, 6) (32, 0) (54, 2). Those widths agree with the types proposed here; where an array or the word 0x808158 is proposed it replaces the typed element rows, and the comments proposed here replace the 'typed ...' comments. | TWIN / COUNTERPART: only the nine bitmap helpers are twins. Round 92's bitfield comments (algorithm_enable_flags_25_t bits 3 and 15, cm550_algorithm_enable_flags_33_t bit 4) call 0x205c4, 0x2041c and 0x20380 'the twin of cm848_...'; the instruction-level comparison here supersedes that: CM848's retarder and fan processors add the DM13 flag (0x40adda) and the monitor inhibit flag (0x40aaca) and the retarder enable sits in another word; CM848's local idle switch fallback adds the armed flag (0x3fbd69) and a forced A/D reading. CM550 has no operand for the DM13 flag, the inhibit flag, the start delay or a multiplex enable bit anywhere in 0x201d6-0x21270 (all absolute operands were listed). | PARALLEL NAMES: two CM550 names differ in their base from CM848's because CM848's under-describe the code; to make the pairs parallel rename CM848 0x50a57c cm848_evaluateJ1939InputSignalFault -> cm848_processJ1939SwitchInput (it also writes the switch state, like its siblings cm848_processJ1939...) and CM848 0x50a4a0 cm848_copyStatusBitToDatalinkSwitch -> cm848_copyOutputBitToSwitchOverrideValue (its 'status bit' is a bit of logical_output_request_bits; CM848's own e2m calls the switch records <switch>_User_Override (block 1575) and <switch>_User_Value 'User override value' (1576), <switch>_Global_Default (1571), <switch>_Inversion (1572) - but 1571-1576 are not in CM848's dumped parameter table, so the address link is not proven). CM848 0x50ae5c cm848_initJ1939InputProcessing -> cm848_initializeJ1939InputProcessing would match the 'initialize' rule. If one base per pair is preferred the other way, cm550_processJ1939SwitchInput / cm550_copyOutputBitToSwitchOverrideValue can take CM848's bases instead. | PREFIX: 0x205c4 gets mc68k_ because it reads the QADC result register table (0xfff2b0 + 2 x index at 0x205f8), the only function besides mc68k_processAnalogSensorChannels that does; if the prefix rule is meant for drivers only, the name is cm550_updateIdleSwitchesFromLocalInputs. The functions that only mask interrupts through SR keep cm550_ (30 cm550_ functions do that). | function_definitions.csv: the parameter rows of 0x201d6 0x20210 0x2024a 0x202d8 0x20310 0x20348 0x20890 carry the old function names; 0x206a8 has the name ptpSwitchedInputDebouncer and the parameters input_state / debounce_mask, which the code shows to be (logical_input, output_number) - argument 1 = (0x14,a7) = the input whose enable, priority and value bit are used, argument 2 = (0x18,a7) = the output image bit and the priority test index. | 0x211f4: no caller found; the start-up list of this ECU is not in the dumped ROM (cm550_initIoControlRegister 0x2481e is also unreferenced). The RAM dump shows 0x800aae = 0 and 0x800aaf = 0 where the function would leave 0xff and 0xf1; that only proves it had not run because both J1939 pedal enables are 0 in this calibration (nothing else then rewrites 0x800aae). So either the undumped code calls it conditionally or nothing calls it. | LEADS, not proposed: (a) 0x201b2-0x201d5, right after the descriptor table: six 6-byte records {timeout slot byte, 0, logical switch dword} = (2,54) (16,11) (15,10) (17,3) (18,1) (19,2) (auxiliary shutdown, brake, clutch, cruise enable / resume / set); no reference in the dumped ROM. (b) 0x80bcf6 (bit_6_which_enables_the_warning_lamp_driver_enable_disable) is byte 0 of the output image 0x80bcf6-0x80bcfb (e2m 000E +28: lamp driver commands bits 0-6, bit 7 the fuel shutoff / pump enable command); the family only proves a bit array indexed by output number, so no name is proposed. (c) Bit 0 of the fault status word 0x806000 (latched in 0x806040) takes all four J1939 multiplexing fault conditions here, where CM848 uses faults 127 / 128 / 129 / 130 and v64t6_s.e2m lists MXPRTMER / MXRTDXER / MXCFER at 1036 +10 bits 0 / 1 / 2; the same bit is written by the two TPU channel 10 speed interrupt handlers (0x19be4, 0x1a644) and the duty cycle monitor (0x1b05a 0x1b17a 0x1b1be). What fault 0 is has not been shown. (d) Logical input 54 is the switch number of descriptor entries 2 (auxiliary shutdown) and 16 (engine derate) and of three of the five output bit copies, as 31 is in CM848's table and calls; v64t6_s.e2m places the auxiliary shutdown priority at 12A8 +3E (62), so this build's numbering is its own. (e) A J1939_SWITCH_STATE enum (0 off, 1 on, 2 error, 3 not available) would fit the 17 j1939_received_*_switch bytes in both firmwares: the code treats 2 and 3 as error / not available everywhere (cmpi.b #3 / #2 at 0x20538 / 0x20572, 0x20a3a / 0x20b1e, 0x20f68). (f) The global rows at 0x80bcda-0x80bce0 are the other bytes of the value array (inputs 16-71) and still carry description names. | Addresses of CM848 data used above: bitmaps 0x3fbd5a / 0x3fbd5e / 0x3fbd62, timer 0x3fbd66, previous state 0x3fbd68, armed flag 0x3fbd69; 12FE 0x5c340; 12F7 0x40aaa6; 12A8 0x40c058. | FALLBACK NAMES IN COMMENTS: the plate comments and global comments use the proposed names; if a fallback is chosen the same swap is needed in them - mc68k_updateIdleSwitchesFromLocalInputs (in the plate comments of 0x20c98 and in the comments of 0x800aac / 0x800aae / 0x800aaf / 0x80bced / 0x80d72c) and switch_input_source_priority[7] / [switch] / [output number] (in the plate comments of 0x204b0, 0x206a8, 0x20890). | VERB PHRASES: the three any...Active names are CM848's reviewed names without the prefix (the twin rule) and are predicates, not verb phrases; that is deliberate. | SCOPE: the describer's scratch directory was not opened; everything here is from the frozen copies, the ROM / RAM images and the e2m files. roles.role: Clears bit N of the long at 0x800aa0 (word index N>>5, bit N&31; and.l with the inverted mask), N being the low byte of its word argument. Every input processor calls it first with its J1939 input number (0, 1, 5, 6, 7, 9 or a descriptor entry's timeout slot).
roles.discriminator: Clear on 0x800aa0, the long whose bit 0x202d8 sets when a received value is in the not-available range (the data error bitmap). 0x2024a is the same code on 0x800aa4 (message timeout bits) and 0x20210 on 0x800aa8 (accelerator input timeout bits); 0x20284 tests this long.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_clearJ1939InputDataErrorBit @ 0x509d98 - TWIN. The PowerPC body does the same steps (word N>>5, mask 1<<(N mod 32), and-not into the long); it is the first of the same nine helpers in the same order (clear +0, +8, +4 / any +0, +8, +4 / set +0, +8, +4 of one static block) and the twin processors call it with the same input numbers. One shared unprefixed name, both rows change.

roles.role: Clears bit N of the long at 0x800aa8. Called with 6, 1 and 7 at the start of the low idle switch (0x204b0), remote accelerator (0x20784) and idle switch pair (0x20e14) processors.
roles.discriminator: Clear on 0x800aa8, the bitmap only the accelerator inputs use: 0x20310 sets a bit when that input's message timed out and 0x202a0 turns the long into the flag byte 0x80d70e (e2m MXACTMER 'PGN timeout error flag for APS/IVS/remote throttle'). Three callers where 0x201d6 / 0x2024a have seven.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_clearJ1939PedalInputTimeoutBit @ 0x509dd8 - TWIN: same code on the +8 long (0x3fbd62), second helper of the block in both; CM848 passes 6 and 7, CM550 also 1 (its remote accelerator processor has no CM848 version).

roles.role: Clears bit N of the long at 0x800aa4. Every input processor calls it beside 0x201d6 with the same input number.
roles.discriminator: Clear on 0x800aa4, the long whose bit N 0x20348 sets when j1939_input_signal_timeouts[N] has counted down to 0 (the message timeout bitmap).
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_clearJ1939InputTimeoutBit @ 0x509e18 - TWIN: same code on the +4 long (0x3fbd5e), third helper of the block in both.

roles.discriminator: Tests 0x800aa8; one caller, and its result goes into a flag byte, not into the fault bit.

roles.role: Returns 1 when the long at 0x800aa4 is not 0, else 0. Both task functions call it after 0x20284 and set or clear the same fault bit 0 of 0x806000 from it.
roles.discriminator: Tests 0x800aa4 (message timeout bits).
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_anyJ1939InputTimeoutActive @ 0x509ed8 - TWIN: same code on the +4 long, called by both task functions after the data error test.

roles.role: J1939 input 5, the engine retarder selection byte (0x80d719): clears data error and timeout bit 5, then - when algorithm enable word 33 bit 4 (0x803cd6 & 0x10) is set and the multiplex priority word 0x808158 is at least the byte 0x80d726 - writes the word 0x80d728 with raw x 4 / 10 for a byte up to 0xFA, else with the default word 0x80815a. A slot 5 timeout sets timeout bit 5 and a not-available byte other than 0xFE sets data error bit 5.
roles.discriminator: Input 5, the retarder byte, scale x4/10 (0.4 % per bit to 1 % per count), output 0x80d728 with default 0x80815a and priority byte 0x80d726; it compares the priority but does not take it. 0x2041c has the same shape for input 0 with x16/10. The dumped ROM has no other reference to 0x80d728 (absolute-long scan and decompiled names).
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_processJ1939EngineRetarderSelection @ 0x509fcc - TWIN: PowerPC body read; same steps in the same order with the same constants (5, 0xFA, 0xFE, x4/10) on the same e2m records (12F7 +D / +1A / +1C, 12FE +0 / +2), called at the same place of the same task. Deltas: CM848 also tests j1939_dm13_fault_log_inhibit_flag and j1939_input_monitor_inhibit_flag before it sets a bit, and its gate (the same Calterm bit ADEBLVOD) is word 13 bit 0 (0x3fd5b6 & 1), not word 33 bit 4.

roles.role: J1939 input 0, the engine fan requested percent speed byte (0x80d71c): clears data error and timeout bit 0, then - when algorithm enable word 25 bit 15 (manual_fan_level_override) is set and the multiplex priority is at least the byte 0x80d727 - writes the word 0x80d72a with raw x 16 / 10 for a byte up to 0xFA, else with the default word 0x80815c. A slot 0 timeout sets timeout bit 0 and a not-available byte other than 0xFE sets data error bit 0.
roles.discriminator: Input 0, the fan request byte, scale x16/10, output 0x80d72a with default 0x80815c and priority byte 0x80d727 (compared, not taken). The dumped ROM has no other reference to 0x80d72a.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_processJ1939EngineFanRequestedSpeed @ 0x50a0cc - TWIN: same steps, same constants (0, 0xFA, 0xFE, x16/10) and the same gate bit (word 25 bit 15 in both) on the same records (12F7 +10 / +1B / +1E, 12FE +4). Delta: CM848's two inhibit-flag guards.

roles.role: J1939 input 6, the 2-bit accelerator pedal low idle switch (0x80d71a): clears data error, timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 6, then - when switch 7's override enable (algorithm enable word 13 bit 7) is set and the multiplex priority is at least switch 7's priority byte 0x80bd51 - takes that priority byte and writes bit 7 of the switch override values 0x80bcd8: the received state for 0 / 1, the global default bit (0x807d6a bit 7) for 2 (error) and 3 (not available, plus data error bit 6). A slot 6 timeout sets timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 6 and leaves the switch alone.
roles.discriminator: Input 6 and logical switch 7 (the idle validation switch) alone; on a timeout it writes no default, unlike 0x20890. 0x20e14 handles the same received byte for switches 7 and 8 together as input 7. The current name cm550_outputControlState1Handler matches nothing in the body: there is no output and no state.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorLowIdleSwitch @ 0x50a1b4 - TWIN: same steps and constants (6, switch 7, values 3 and 2, default bit 7, no switch write on timeout), first callee of the accelerator task in both. Deltas: CM848 calls cm848_set / clearDatalinkSwitchStateIfPriority(7, 0) where CM550 has that test inlined (it writes only while the priority byte is 0), tests j1939_input_monitor_inhibit_flag, and takes the enable from switch_input_datalink_source_bits_cal[0] & 0x80.

roles.role: Local fallback for the idle switch pair: with algorithm enable word 25 bit 3 set it copies the sampled throttle's raw QADC result into 0x80d72c and treats more than 360 counts as off idle; otherwise it debounces the hardware not-idle switch (raw port byte 0x80bced XOR the inversion byte 0x800aaf, bit 0; timer 0x800aac = 100 on a change, minus 50 per pass, accepted at 0). It then writes switch 7 (idle, 0x80bcd8 bit 7), switch 8 (not idle, 0x80bcd9 bit 0) and the off-idle word 0x80aa86.
roles.discriminator: Called only by 0x20c98, when the J1939 pedal message has timed out. The only function of the family that reads local hardware (a QADC result register and the raw switch port image) and no received J1939 byte; it writes the two override bits with no priority test and touches no fault bitmap. Sole user of the statics 0x800aac / 0x800aae / 0x800aaf besides the initializer.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_updateIdleSwitchesFromLocalInputs @ 0x50a2cc - TWIN (medium): the same two branches on the same bit (word 25 bit 3), the same constants (360 counts, 100, 50, switches 7 and 8), the same single caller (the pedal position processor on timeout). Deltas: CM848 re-arms the timer through accelerator_idle_switch_debounce_armed_flag, can use a forced A/D reading, reads the switch with cm848_readSwitchHardwareInput(8) (line XOR polarity bit, which CM550 does inline with a cached byte) and writes through the priority-0 helpers where CM550 writes unconditionally. If those deltas are judged to break the twin rule: cm550_updateIdleSwitchesFromLocalInputs.

roles.role: Takes two long arguments (switch number, output number): when the switch's override enable bit is set (bit 0xD0 + switch of the algorithm enable words, i.e. word 13 onward) and the multiplex priority is at least the priority byte indexed by the OUTPUT number (0x80bd4a + output), it takes the switch's own priority byte and, only if that byte is then 0, copies bit 'output' of the output image 0x80bcf6 into bit 'switch' of the switch override values (0x80bcd8 bit array).
roles.discriminator: The only function whose source is an output command bit, not a received J1939 byte or a hardware input; no timeout slot and no fault bit. 0x21070 calls it five times with (54,1) (54,4) (33,6) (32,0) (54,2); inputs 32 / 33 are the lamp 1 / lamp 2 feedback inputs (e2m 12A8 +20 / +21) and outputs 0-6 the lamp drivers (e2m 12A7).
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_copyStatusBitToDatalinkSwitch @ 0x50a4a0 - TWIN: same steps in the same order, including the same odd priority read indexed by the output bit instead of the switch (CM848's plate comment calls it a slip), and the same caller position (five calls after the retarder processor; CM848's pairs are (31,1) (31,35) (31,0) (4,4) (31,5)). CM848's source array is logical_output_request_bits, so the 'status bit' of its name is an output request bit; the suggested shared name says that (the plain alternative is copyStatusBitToDatalinkSwitch).

roles.role: J1939 remote accelerator pedal position (byte 0x80d722): clears data error, timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 1, then - when remote_throttle_enable (word 18 bit 12) and the remote throttle switch override enable (word 14 bit 3) are set and the multiplex priority is at least A/D channel 11's override priority word 0x80a6e0 - writes analog_sensor_override_values[11] with raw x 16 / 10 for a byte up to 0xFA (clearing fault bit 0 of 0x806000), else with remote_throttle_sensor_config.default_value. A slot 1 timeout sets timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 1, 0xFE sets fault bit 0 with its first-occurrence latch, and 0xFB-0xFD / 0xFF set data error bit 1.
roles.discriminator: Target A/D channel 11 (remote throttle) and bit / slot 1 - the slot of the EBC1 remote accelerator enable switch, although the EEC2 handler reloads slot 8 for this byte; descriptor entry 14 (that enable switch) drives the same bit 1 of the data error and timeout bitmaps from the other task. Unlike 0x20c98 and 0x20fac it does not store the multiplex priority into the channel's priority word, and it is the only processor that clears the fault bit on a valid value.
roles.cm848_counterpart: none: CM848's EEC2 handler stores j1939_received_remote_accelerator_pedal_position, but no CM848 function reads it (one hit in the .cpp, the store) and nothing tests timeout slot 1 or 8 outside the descriptor loop; its accelerator task calls three processors where CM550 calls five.

roles.role: Processes entry i of j1939_input_signal_descriptor_table (17 ten-byte entries: received byte pointer, timeout slot, logical switch): clears the slot's timeout and data error bits, then - when the switch's override enable bit is set and the multiplex priority is at least the switch's priority byte (0x80bd4a + switch) - takes that priority byte and, while it is 0, writes the switch's override value bit (0x80bcd8 bit array). The bit is the received 2-bit state for 0 / 1 and the switch's global default bit (longs at 0x807d6a) on a timeout (plus the timeout bit), on 3 (plus the data error bit) and on 2.
roles.discriminator: The only table-driven processor: input byte, slot and switch come from the descriptor entry given as the argument (0-16, from 0x21070); the other processors hard-code theirs. It clears the timeout bit before the data error bit, the reverse of the others.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_evaluateJ1939InputSignalFault @ 0x50a57c - TWIN: same steps in the same order (also timeout bit before data error bit), same 10-byte entries and values 3 / 2; the two tables match pointer for pointer and slot for slot. Deltas: CM848's two inhibit-flag guards and its non-inlined priority-0 helpers; its default bits are bytes, CM550's longs. The CM848 base name covers only the fault half, while the body's main result is the switch state, hence the suggested shared name (the plain alternative is evaluateJ1939InputSignalFault).

roles.role: J1939 input 7, accelerator pedal position 1 (byte 0x80d714): when the sampled throttle override enable (word 5 bit 10) and switch 7's override enable (word 13 bit 7) are set and the multiplex priority is at least A/D channel 10's priority word 0x80a6de, it takes that priority word and writes analog_sensor_override_values[10] (raw x 16 / 10 with the off-idle word 0x80aa86 = raw != 0 for a byte up to 0xFA, else sampled_throttle_sensor_config.default_value). A slot 7 timeout sets timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 7 and runs the local fallback 0x205c4; 0xFE sets fault bit 0 and, when the low idle switch is 0 or 1, the flag 0x80d70c with off-idle taken from the switch; other not-available bytes set data error bit 7.
roles.discriminator: Target A/D channel 10 (sampled throttle), with ownership of its priority word; the only caller of 0x205c4 and the only writer of the flag 0x80d70c; while the flag 0x80d70d is set it discards a valid pedal value. It clears no bitmap bits itself (0x20e14 does that for input 7 just before it).
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorPedalPosition @ 0x50a700 - TWIN (medium): same decision tree and constants (7, 0xFA, 0xFE, x16/10, low idle switch 2 / 1) on the same 12F7 records (+0, +1, +8) with the same fallback call. Deltas: CM848 has a DM13 branch and the inhibit-flag guards, clears accelerator_idle_switch_debounce_armed_flag, and uses its own fault bit with a registered copy where CM550 uses fault bit 0 of 0x806000; the target is channel 13's held_value there, channel 10's override word here. If those deltas are judged to break the twin rule: cm550_processJ1939AcceleratorPedalPosition.

roles.role: The switch half of J1939 input 7: clears data error, timeout and accelerator-timeout bit 7, then - under the same two enables as 0x20c98 and with the multiplex priority at least the priority bytes of switches 7 and 8 (0x80bd51, 0x80bd52) - takes both priority bytes and, unless the flag 0x80d70e is set, writes both override bits from the low idle switch byte 0x80d71a: switch 7 = the state and switch 8 = its inverse for 0 / 1, both global default bits for 2 and 3. A 2 also sets fault bit 0 with its latch; a 3 sets the flag 0x80d70d and data error bit 7.
roles.discriminator: Writes the pair of switches 7 and 8 (idle and not idle) from one received byte; the only function of the family that tests 0x80d70e and the only one that sets 0x80d70d. 0x204b0 handles switch 7 alone as input 6 with a different enable set.
roles.cm848_counterpart: cm848_processJ1939AcceleratorIdleSwitchPair @ 0x50a9d4 - TWIN: same steps and constants (7, switches 7 and 8, values 2 and 3, the same 12F7 +1 / +2 flags), same place between the low idle switch and pedal position processors. Deltas: CM848's inhibit-flag guards, its priority-0 helpers, its own fault bit.

roles.role: J1939 input 9, the wet tank pressure byte (0x80d720): clears data error and timeout bit 9, then - when algorithm enable word 20 bit 9 is set and the multiplex priority is at least the word 0x80a6fc - takes that priority word and writes the word 0x80a760 with raw x 9282 / 100 for a byte up to 0xFA, else with the word 0x806d3c. A slot 9 timeout sets timeout bit 9 and a not-available byte other than 0xFE sets data error bit 9.

blind.notes: MODULE. CM550 0x201d6-0x211f4 is the same source module as CM848's J1939 multiplexed input layer 0x509d98-0x50ae5c: the functions come in the same order in both (nine bit helpers, retarder, fan, low idle switch, local idle fallback, output copy, descriptor entry, pedal position, idle switch pair, switch task, accelerator task, initializer) and CM550 has two more processors in between (0x20784 remote accelerator, 0x20fac wet tank pressure) that CM848 lacks although it still receives both bytes. The layer acts as one override client: it compares the priority word 0x808158 with each input's client priority, then writes switch override bits, A/D channel override words or the two request words. | TWIN RULE USED. Twin = the same decision tree in the same order with the same logic constants (input numbers, 0xFA / 0xFE, 2-bit values 3 and 2, x4/10, x16/10, 360 counts, 100 / 50) at the same place in the call graph. Allowed deltas: guards only CM848 has (j1939_dm13_fault_log_inhibit_flag, j1939_input_monitor_inhibit_flag, j1939_multiplex_enable, j1939_input_fault_start_delay), CM550 inlining the priority-0 switch write helper, and each firmware's own addresses, calibration bit, fault bit, switch and output numbers. The frozen CSVs hold a precedent on each side of that line: writeJ1939DiagnosticMemory (CM848 0x50af58 / CM550 0x2148a: one shared name although CM550 returns another code and has no refresh-window refusal and no Bank 2) and cm550_tickJ1939InputSupervision (0x21edc, the tick of this same layer: labelled a counterpart of 0x50bca0 because most of CM848's body - gate, start delay, start-up timer, inhibit flag - is logic CM550 lacks before the one shared loop). The four medium twins (0x205c4, 0x20c98, 0x21070, 0x21146) sit on the twin side because nearly all of both bodies is the shared sequence and the rest is guards or bookkeeping for a feature one firmware lacks; each entry lists its deltas and the cm550_ fallback name in case 'same steps' is read strictly. 0x211f4 sits on the other side: three of its four statements match CM848's initializer, each side has effects the other lacks, and its call site is not in the dump, so the call-graph half of the proof is missing. | FAULT BIT. Every error path and both summaries use bit 0 of the system error status word 0x806000 with the first-occurrence word 0x806040, under an interrupt mask (move sr / ori #0x700). e2m block 1036 +0 has S records for masks 0x02-0x10 but none for 0x01; the same bit is also set and cleared by mc68k_tpuChannel10PrimarySpeedInterruptHandlerMode0 / Mode2 and mc68k_dutyCycleMonitorIsrHandler, and fault number 0 is what the unused tri-state fault fields of all 25 sensor configs hold. It looks like an unassigned fault number; the code does not prove that. In both tasks the 'any timeout' summary overwrites the 'any data error' summary (CM848 uses two bits), so a data error alone leaves only the first-occurrence bit set. | INACTIVE, NOT DEAD. In the RAM dump every gate is clear (algorithm enable words 5, 13, 14, 16, 20, 33 = 0; word 25 = 0x0180 with bits 3 and 15 clear; only word 18 bit 12 remote_throttle_enable is set), the three bitmaps are 0 and 0x808158 is 0. | OTHER FINDINGS. verdict.overall:
I judged J1 against the frozen copies. Evidence: my own CPU32 and PowerPC disassembly of both layers (CM550 0x201d6-0x21270, CM848 0x509d98-0x50aec0), abs_refs, the ECU parameter ID table, the e2m records and the main and extended RAM dumps.

FUNCTIONS. The nine bitmap helpers are step-for-step twins: same index N>>5, same mask 1<<(N&31), and/or into the +0/+4/+8 dwords, the same one-pass 'any' loop quirk and the same order of the nine. Six keep the proposed shared names. The three 'any...Active' predicates are AMENDED to isAny...: the rule asks for a verb phrase, they are the only predicates in either CSV without is/has/are/check, and both rows change anyway.

Every processor, both tasks and the initializer are COUNTERPARTS, as the investigator says, not twins as the describer says.
